name: single mu-/mu+
description: One muon per event, charge drawn per event from {mu-, mu+} with equal probability. Kinetic energy uniform in [200, 2000] MeV, isotropic direction. The two charges are NOT equivalent here even though the Cherenkov light is: mu- captures on oxygen, mu+ does not, so a stopping mu+ always yields its decay electron while a stopping mu- sometimes loses it. A single-charge test set therefore misstates how often the delayed signal is present. Expressed through the bomb source with min_particles = max_particles = 1 -- a two-entry `particles` list would put BOTH charges in every event (generate_macro.py emits one /gun/addPrimary per entry), which is not the same sample.
